# Superjump

**One sentence:** Jumper's original structure — read the problem, take it apart, leap into a foreign domain, resolve the contradiction, kill the weak ideas — watched for real progress instead of cut off by a clock, with every idea judged in your brief's own terms.

**Status:** shipped. Run `node bin/superjump-run.mjs --input brief.txt`. Jumper lean remains the fast path; Superjump is the original structure, watched for progress, judged in the brief's own terms.

## Use this when
- You want genuinely new ideas, not the first three sensible ones (that is Jumper's lean mode)
- You can say what "good" means, or you want the engine to show you what it took "good" to mean
- You want to see why an idea lost, in the brief's own terms, and re-weigh the survivors yourself

## What you get, in this order
- The Fit Contract the run aimed at, each item with the line of your brief it came from: the deliverable, the must-haves, the fixed facts, the forbids, the judging axes (yours if you wrote a JUDGE line, derived otherwise)
- Survivors ordered by anchored ratings on those axes, each with its deliverable, the one-line mechanism that makes it different, the foreign domain it leapt through and the trace of what it borrowed, its eligibility table with the passages that prove it, any uncertain flags, and the smallest fair test (unperformed)
- Kills with the explicit term that killed them and the passage; anything still in flight or unjudged, named as such
- Duplicates grouped as one idea with two routes, never counted twice
- Timings: when the first reviewed idea arrived, when the portfolio was complete, and what each seat cost

## How to write the brief (optional lines the engine honours)
```
DELIVERABLE: three endings, each with beats, sacrifice, enforcement
MUST: the children act; Corvo cannot simply repeat the attack next morning
FIXED: school year September–June; Riley has two loan laptops
FORBID: wire ceremony; portal; adult-won fight
JUDGE: human benefit 3; children's agency 3; believable safety 2; simplicity 1
```
After a run you can change the JUDGE weights and re-order the same results without paying for another run.

## The clock, honestly
- There is no time limit. The run tells you what to expect from measured runs, watches each seat for real signs of work, and writes its results as they land, so you can read what exists at any moment.
- If a seat shows no observable progress well beyond the range runs have finished in, the run says so and recommends a kill, naming what has landed and what a kill would forfeit. The decision is yours or the steward's; the engine never kills on a clock. The only automatic stop is a generous safety timeout against a hung process, recorded in the run.
- At the highest model effort the full structure takes longer than ten minutes on today's measurements; the first wave measures what to expect, and every run records what it ran at.

## Do not use this when
- You need a diagnosis of an existing artifact (Gandalf)
- You need a build plan (Crucible) or a build (Foreman)
- You want quick vetted options in a few minutes (Jumper lean)

## Limits (honest)
- The independent review fails closed if the second model family is down
- Fit is judgment with passages plus a few labelled lint checks, not proof that an idea works
- A rating is only as good as the contract; read the contract first
- On the first two live briefs (Einstein finite-cover; Book 1 endings), foreign-domain leaps often produced the same idea in different clothes. Superjump is not yet shown to be more novel than Jumper lean. Keep using it and judge later runs on distinctness, not costume.
